clue.text: Recoil from black cat

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: Someone jumps back in alarm from a black cat crossing their path.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce, or snow leopard, is a crossword favourite for 'cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to spring back, and a ball does exactly that when it rebounds off a wall.

clue.text: Forbids leader to excuse supporting ambassador’s howler

indicators.note: the leader belonging to a word is its opening letter, so only that one letter is kept
in a down entry a piece that supports another sits underneath it in the grid

blocks.note: to forbid is to ban
HE, His Excellency, is the formal title of an ambassador
the first letter of excuse

explanation.surface: An ambassador blunders and is barred from making excuses for the gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Howler' looks like a blunder, fitting the diplomatic scene, but it means a wailer: BANS + HE + E, with the E placed below HE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a banshee is a female spirit whose wailing cry foretells a death, so she is literally a howler.

clue.text: For the most part unrewarded, cracked combinations

indicators.note: most but not all of the following word is used, so its final letter is dropped
something cracked is broken apart, so its letters fall into a fresh order

blocks.note: the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: Code-crackers go mostly unpaid for breaking safe combinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combinations' suggests safe codes, but it is an old name for a one-piece undergarment covering body and legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Combinations were a one-piece garment of vest and long drawers, worn beneath clothes, so they are a kind of underclothing.

clue.text: Settlement of intestine requiring surgery in the end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so that single letter is kept

blocks.note: the colon is the large intestine
the final letter of surgery

explanation.surface: A patient's bowel trouble is finally settled by an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a group of people who settle in a new land, so it names a settlement.

clue.text: One on board ship seized by revolutionary worker

indicators.note: whatever is seized is held inside its captor, so one piece is gripped within the other

blocks.note: Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary
SS stands for steamship
a man is a worker or hand

explanation.surface: A ship is commandeered by a rebellious crewman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a sailor on a vessel, but the board here is a chequered one for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess piece such as a knight or bishop is one of the figures standing on the playing board.

clue.text: Hampshire’s opener gets duck with fine catch

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, so only that one is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of Hampshire
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, which looks like the letter O
fine means OK

explanation.surface: Hampshire's opening batsman is out for nothing but takes a good catch in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is an English county with a cricket team, and the cricket scene hides the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook is a curved fastening that catches and holds, and a catch on a door is the same kind of device.

clue.text: Great seeing special student finish papers

blocks.note: SP is a dictionary abbreviation for special
L is a learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car
to finish is to end
ID papers prove who you are

explanation.surface: It is great to see a special-needs student complete their written exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid and great are both informal words of enthusiastic approval for something excellent.

clue.text: Under obligation after Mike cut the grass

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other, fixing their order left to right

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
something owed is a debt you are obliged to pay

explanation.surface: Someone feeling indebted to Mike does the gardening for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Mowing is trimming a lawn with a mower, so the past tense describes a lawn that has been trimmed.

clue.text: Market garden runs analysis on rye variety

indicators.note: analysis breaks something down into parts, so the letters are taken apart and rebuilt
a variety is a different form, so these letters appear in another order
in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A market garden tests which strain of rye grows best.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant nursery is a commercial place where young plants and trees are raised for sale, much like a market garden.

clue.text: Lump has to drop off then you’ll report

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the words are to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: to drop off is to nod off to sleep
the contraction said out loud

explanation.surface: A lump has to fall off eventually, and then you'll file a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop off' looks like the lump falling away; it means falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodule is a small rounded swelling or growth, in the body or in rock, which is exactly a little lump.

clue.text: Fan of Orwell work

indicators.note: to work something is to shape it, so the letters before it are reshaped

blocks.note: every letter of both words is used

explanation.surface: An admirer of one of George Orwell's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a book by Orwell; it tells you to rework the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is a devoted supporter, and a follower is someone who supports and keeps up with a person or team.

clue.text: Hurry to question writer endlessly

indicators.note: without its ends, so the first and last letters are removed

blocks.note: QU is a standard abbreviation for question
Charles Dickens, the Victorian novelist

explanation.surface: Rush to put endless questions to an author.
explanation.definitionFit: To quicken is to make faster or speed up, which is what it means to hurry something along.

clue.text: Managed to stop a huge angry tirade

indicators.note: something angry is stirred up and agitated, so these letters are thrown into a new order
a stopper plugs a gap, so this piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to manage a business is to run it

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in cutting short a huge, furious rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managed' looks like coping, but it means ran, as in running a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long, loud, aggressive speech, which is the same as a ranting tirade.

clue.text: Nervous about creep

blocks.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
to edge is to creep forward slowly

explanation.surface: Feeling jittery about a sinister creep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creep' looks like a nasty person; here it is the verb to inch along.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for feeling tense, jumpy and anxious.

clue.text: Fighter, with terrible roar, tackling Irish uprising

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters of the next word come out jumbled
rising up in a down entry means reading from bottom to top
to tackle someone is to wrap your arms around them

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A fighter with a fearsome war cry takes on an Irish rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrior is a brave soldier or combatant, someone whose trade is fighting.

clue.text: Enthralled by education in the past, you studied

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so this piece is held within the other

blocks.note: ED is the abbreviation for education
ye is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: You were spellbound by your schooling and worked hard at your books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studied' looks like learning, but it is the past tense of study in the sense of looking closely at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something can mean to look at it carefully, and eyed means looked at closely.

clue.text: Just managing with son at home eating rubbish grub. Disheartened? Yes

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece is placed within another
losing the heart means the middle goes, leaving only the two outside letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
crap is slang for rubbish
at home means in
the outside letters of grub
Y stands for yes, as on a Y/N form

explanation.surface: A family barely coping, with the son at home eating junk food and feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' looks like the son's mood, but it works on the word grub, cutting out its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraping by is an idiom for surviving with barely enough money, which is just about managing.

clue.text: Lose interest with half of government going round idle

indicators.note: half of a word means only its first half of letters is kept
going round something encircles it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the first five of the ten letters
to idle is to laze

explanation.surface: Voters switch off as half the government drifts around doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: When eyes glaze over they go blank and unfocused, the look of someone who has become bored.

clue.text: Most sugary foods finally getting negligible tax

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it, so only its last letter is used

blocks.note: the last letter of foods
wee means tiny
to tax someone is to test or strain them

explanation.surface: The sweetest foods eventually face a small sugar tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks like a levy, fitting the sugar-tax story, but it is the verb meaning to strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetest is the superlative of sweet, describing whatever contains the greatest amount of sugar.

clue.text: Fruit with unsightly growths recalled, make a mistake by accepting

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the word is read in the backward direction
to accept is to take in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: warts are unsightly growths on the skin
taken as written
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A batch of blemished fruit is recalled after someone's error.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry is a soft red summer fruit with seeds on the outside of its skin.

clue.text: Academic child’s also crazy about reading

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters before it are scrambled

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for child
taken as written
reading is one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A bookish child who is mad about reading.
explanation.walkthrough: CH and ALSO are jumbled and R joins at the end; 'about' here loosely means on the subject of. The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person, especially one engaged in university study and research, which is an academic.

clue.text: Briefly turned up bringing in money collected

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the word loses its final letter
bringing something in takes it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: someone who turned up came
L is the pound sign, standing for money

explanation.surface: Someone dropped by briefly to bring in cash that had been gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collected' looks like gathered money, but it is the adjective meaning composed.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected person is self-possessed and composed, which is to say unflustered and serene.

clue.text: Nonsense chit-chat from mummy bird leading young

indicators.note: the leading letter of a word is the one at the front, so only that is kept

blocks.note: ma is a child's word for mother
the lark is a songbird
the first letter of young

explanation.surface: A mother bird chirps idle nonsense at her chicks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummy' looks like an Egyptian mummy or a mother bird, but it is just MA. This is a less common spelling of a word usually written with an extra E.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarkey is informal for foolish, meaningless talk, so it names silly, empty chatter.

clue.text: Guide key soldiers back to front

indicators.note: the back belonging to a word is its last letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the escape key on a computer keyboard
OR means other ranks, ordinary soldiers
the final letter of front

explanation.surface: A guide sends key troops from the rear up to the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to front' looks like a reversal instruction; it only picks the last letter of front.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to accompany and lead them somewhere, which is what a guide does.

clue.text: A hex or trick reveals prankster

indicators.note: a trick deceives, so the letters before it are disguised in a new order

blocks.note: every letter of the three words is used

explanation.surface: Casting a curse or playing a trick exposes the joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoaxer deceives people with practical jokes or fake stories, which is what a prankster does.

clue.text: Run out after badly written gag’s hostile reaction

indicators.note: something badly written has its letters set down wrongly, so they appear out of order
one piece follows the other, fixing their order

blocks.note: taken as written
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A comedian's clumsily scripted joke drives the audience out in anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive, troublesome behaviour or animosity, short for aggravation.

clue.text: With Spring coming on female deer thrives

blocks.note: a doe is a female deer
a spring is a well, a source of water

explanation.surface: As spring arrives, the female deer flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, but it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does well prospers or succeeds, which is what it means to thrive.

clue.text: Judge has low sufferance for cheek

indicators.note: suffering knocks something about, so the letters before it are disturbed

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge has little tolerance for insolence in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' looks like impudence, fitting the courtroom, but it means the side of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A jowl is the lower part of the face, the fleshy area of the jaw and lower cheek.

clue.text: Signed in to record professor in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken aloud, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: to record is to log, and a professor is a don, a university teacher; the two words run together when spoken

explanation.surface: Someone signed up to tape a lecturer's talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Don is the traditional name for an Oxford or Cambridge university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Logging on means entering a password to access a computer system, which is signing in.

clue.text: Only one securing victory’s right for you

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: sole means only one
V is for victory
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A lone winner claiming their prize sounds like the right result.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside SOLE, then R follows. The definition addresses you, the person tackling the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone working out a crossword is its solver, so the setter's 'you' fits the reader exactly.

clue.text: Jumper fellow left during match is found on top of building

definitions.note: a phrase describing the thing, not a noun

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
F is the abbreviation for fellow
a tie is a match or fixture in a cup competition
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A sweater left behind by a fellow at a game turns up on a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, which in Britain is a jumper, but it is the leaping kangaroo. L goes inside TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof tile is one of the overlapping slates or clay plates covering the top of a house.

clue.text: Alternative energy source in farm building floor

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so only the opening letter is used
placed in something means inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a sty is a pig pen
or introduces an alternative
the first letter of energy

explanation.surface: Renewable power is generated in a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative energy source' reads as one phrase, like solar panels, but it splits into three separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level of a building, so it is another word for a floor.
